normalized_symbol_note: The reconstructed C++ symbol is the Ghidra name verbatim. Nothing descriptive is appended: the record name and the source symbol are the same token, which is also what lets the validator bind the source span to this VA deterministically. The name embeds the 8-hex target VA 004adc40.

abi.ghidra_convention_discrepancy: Ghidra decompiles the single register parameter as __fastcall int param_1. The body consumes ECX only: EDX is never read, no stack slot is read, and the body ends in a bare RET. The machine ABI is therefore identical to __thiscall with no parameters, and staging declares __thiscall.
abi.return_type_note: Field is this package's std::uint8_t alias, declared in adc40_flag.hpp. The 1-byte width is machine-derived from the byte-wide load MOV AL,byte ptr [EAX+0x4f] and corroborated by three call sites that consume AL alone.
abi.return_semantics: Returns the unsigned byte stored at receiver+0x4F. In the original only AL is written, so the upper 24 bits of EAX are NOT zero-extended: they retain receiver address bits 8..31 because EAX was reloaded from the spilled ECX immediately before the byte load. Consumers must read AL only; all three sampled call sites do. The reconstructed source returns a std::uint8_t and therefore zero-extends, which is a strictly stronger guarantee; see source_fidelity.
abi.return_register_upper_bits: indeterminate-by-construction, equal to receiver address bits 8..31
abi.frame: Original encoding only: PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / PUSH ECX / MOV [EBP-0x4],ECX prologue with MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP / RET epilogue. The PUSH ECX spill to [EBP-0x4] and the reload from it are redundant; no instruction in the body ever reads that slot other than the reload itself. The reconstruction does not reproduce the frame; see source_fidelity.

source_fidelity.summary: The reconstruction claims the machine-observable semantics of the body, not its instruction encoding. The original is 17 bytes in 9 instructions; the reconstruction emits 5 bytes in 2 instructions.
reproduced: Receiver in ECX, no stack argument, bare RET, caller owns stack cleanup.
Exactly one byte-wide load from receiver+0x4f.
No write to the receiver, no call, no branch, no allocation, no guard.
not_reproduced: The PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / PUSH ECX / spill / reload prologue and its symmetric epilogue. The compiler emits no frame for a function this small.

The un-zero-extended upper 24 bits of EAX. A C++ function returning std::uint8_t is free to zero-extend, and the emitted MOVZBL does. This is a stronger guarantee than the original made, not a weaker one, and no sampled consumer depends on the difference.
The 17-byte length and the specific opcode encodings, which are assembler choices.
source_fidelity.why_not_inline_asm: A naked inline-assembly body was built and rejected. GCC models i386 __attribute__((thiscall)) with a callee-popped argument area: at -O2 the call site emits a compensating 'sub $0x8,%esp' after the call, which a naked body ending in a bare RET (c3) never consumes, so every caller returned through a corrupted stack. Reproducing the encoding exactly would have meant shipping a function that cannot be called. The plain form builds warning-free under -Wall -Wextra -Werror and its model test passes at -O0, -O1, -O2 and -Os.

body.describes: the original body at 0x004adc40, read from the live Ghidra bridge; not the encoding the reconstruction emits
mechanics: ECX supplies the receiver and is spilled to the EBP-0x4 local, then reloaded into EAX.
The body performs exactly one byte-wide load from receiver+0x4F into AL.
No byte of the receiver is written; the function is a pure read.
The body contains no branch, no call, no allocation, no reference-count operation, no ownership transfer and no guard.

receiver_layout.declaration: struct alignas(4) OpaqueEditorFlag { Byte opaque_000[0x4f]; Byte byte_04f; };
receiver_layout.type_identity_note: The briefing assigns subsystem Editor and Ghidra names two of the 64 direct callers Editors::cEditor::sub_581F70 and Editors::cEditor::OnMouseDown. Two sampled call sites load the receiver from a +0x28 member of the caller's own object, but a third samples it from a stack local, so the receiver is a general opaque object pointer and no concrete SDK type is promoted here. The declared layout models the 0x4f byte and the padding below it only; it asserts nothing about any byte at or above 0x50.

sampled_call_sites.result_use: MOVZX EDX, AL; TEST EDX, EDX; JZ
MOVZX EAX, AL; TEST EAX, EAX; JZ

consumer_contract.agreement: All three sampled sites consume only AL and then test it for zero, which independently corroborates the one-byte return width and the non-zero-extended upper EAX bits.

null_and_mutation_behavior.null_receiver: No guard exists; a null receiver performs an unchecked byte load at address 0x4F and faults.
null_and_mutation_behavior.near_null_receiver: No range or alignment guard exists; a near-null receiver faults when receiver+0x4F is inaccessible.
null_and_mutation_behavior.null_field_value: A stored zero byte returns zero in AL.
null_and_mutation_behavior.high_field_value: A stored 0xFF byte returns 0xFF in AL; the load is not masked or narrowed.
null_and_mutation_behavior.mutation: No receiver or field byte is written.

call_graph.consumer_boundary: The high fan-in and the Editor/creature, diplomacy and model clusters in the caller set indicate a broadly used predicate byte, but fan-in alone does not prove that every caller passes the same concrete receiver type.

evidence.observation: Live function range is 0x004adc40 through 0x004adc50, size 17 bytes.
Nine instructions matching the raw bytes; MOV AL,byte ptr [EAX + 0x4f] establishes a one-byte field read at offset 0x4F.
Live decompilation is return *(undefined1 *)(param_1 + 0x4f) under an __fastcall int param_1 label.
Call site 0x00435aa5 loads ECX from [ECX+0x28] and consumes the result as MOVZX EDX,AL; TEST EDX,EDX.
Call site 0x0043ffd2 loads ECX from [EDX+0x28] and consumes the result as MOVZX EAX,AL; TEST EAX,EAX.
Call site 0x00588ba6 inside Editors::cEditor::OnMouseDown loads ECX from a stack local and consumes the result as TEST AL,AL.

Two direct callers carry SDK-derived names, Editors::cEditor::sub_581F70 @ 0x00582250 and Editors::cEditor::OnMouseDown @ 0x00588570, supporting the Editor subsystem label without fixing the receiver type.
Ghidra reports no callees, no referenced vtables and 76 function code xrefs.

verification_results.x86_32_build: passed; g++ -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror builds clean with no warnings at -O0, -O1, -O2 and -Os
verification_results.focused_model_test: passed at all four optimisation levels
verification_results.exhaustive_byte_sweep: passed; all 256 stored byte values round-trip exactly, including 0x80 and 0xff which a signed or narrowed reading would get wrong
verification_results.read_only: passed; the receiver is compared byte-for-byte before and after the call and is unchanged
verification_results.byte_width_isolation: passed; with every byte below 0x4f set to 0xff and the field to 0x00 the call returns 0x00, and with a larger arena whose bytes past the declared extent are 0xff the result still tracks only byte_04f
verification_results.null_and_near_null_fault_tests: passed in forked child processes; both die with SIGSEGV, confirming there is no guard
verification_results.emitted_code: movzbl 0x4f(%ecx),%eax ; ret -- receiver in ECX, byte-wide load at 0x4f, bare ret, 5 bytes
verification_results.caller_abi: passed; call sites load the receiver into ECX and perform no stack adjustment after the call, matching the original's caller-cleanup contract
verification_results.instruction_parity: not claimed; the reconstruction emits 2 instructions against the original's 9. The semantics are reproduced, the encoding is not. See source_fidelity.
verification_results.byte_encoding_parity: not claimed; the reconstruction emits 5 bytes against the original's 17. See source_fidelity.
verification_results.return_register_upper_bits: not asserted by the model test; a C++ uint8_t return zero-extends, so the test pins the low byte and deliberately does not pin bits 8..31

Is the +0x4F byte a bool, a small enum, or a bitfield-style flags byte? Callers only ever test it for zero, so the evidence cannot separate these.
Do all 64 direct callers pass the same concrete receiver type, given the +0x28-member and stack-local receiver provenances already observed?
Which owner constructs and publishes receivers for this accessor?
What values are observed at receiver+0x4F in the original process?
